column1: # Game profile of Assassin's Creed III Remastered (Switch, base game 1.0.0 = v0). Provisional: never run on a device yet
# Ubisoft's AnvilNext (the "scimitar" runtime), SDK 5.4.0, NVN. Modules main + subsdk1 (GLSLC, NVN's runtime shader compiler) + subsdk2 (NintendoSDK_movie) + sdk.
# subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_OpenGL) is not loaded: main imports nothing from it, and the host answers its EGL imports where a game uses them. The NROs in nro/ import
# from subsdk2, so the movie module is loaded as well. RomFS: 265 files in ac3/, acl/, videos/, nro/ and .nrr/, 11.65 GB.
# The game compiles shaders at run time with its own GLSLC (main imports glslcCompile; the NROs call it too), so those outputs are captured on the device during
# Build (the glslc_capture group below), as for Fire Emblem: Three Houses. No static shader table is available yet.
# Written from the survey of the user's own dump (scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py / dm/games/profile_guess.py) and checked against the game files; README.md beside this file.
# guess: a 3D action game with a free camera on the right stick; no file decides it
# main takes nothing from subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_OpenGL); the NROs import from subsdk2 (NintendoSDK_movie)
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region. Not measured on a device yet.
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon
# glslc_capture: the outputs the game's own GLSLC makes at run time, captured during Build (hle_glslc.c); the rest is what shader_split.py finds in the RomFS
